title: Professional Analysts Follow AI Agent Lean 86% of the Time in Anthropic Study
summary:
The AI research firm conducted a behavioral study to determine whether skilled human workers maintain their independence when delegating complex workloads to automated assistants. In a randomized trial involving 50 professional data analysts, participants adopted the AI agent's recommendation 86% of the time, significantly higher than the 50% rate that would occur if the AI had no impact on the analysts' judgment. The agent was instructed to provide honest cases for its options and was told to change its position if the evidence required it.

The results indicate that AI assistants can bias the final decision making of the experts they support, even when those users believe they are acting independently. Industry observers noted the findings highlight a need for professionals to be deliberate about when in their process they integrate AI tools to ensure that independent judgment is not compromised by the positions of the AI agent.
